WHAT YOU NEED TO DO
Use Your Resources
Remember: resources are more than money!
Focus on your strengths.
Focus on your interests.
Don't forget your social networks they can bring resources too!
Look for new resources, don't wait for them to appear!
Matthew 25: 14-30
• The Parable of the Talents teaches that God always gives us everything we
need to do what he has called us to do.
3

o Strengths - List 5 which you are good at
o Interests - List 5 you really like doing
o Other resources - List 5 (e.g. your social or financial

Instruction:
1. Think about...
o 5 notable strengths (which you are good at),
o 5 interests (what you like to do), and
o 5 other resources (e.g. your social or financial
resources)
2. Now try to create 2 business ideas that include (at least)
one of your strengths, one of your interests and one of
your other resources. Present your ideas to your partner.
3. What more could you do (based on your resources) to be
unique?
EXERCISE: Your Strengths, Your
Interests & Other Resources
WS
12
Example:
Julienne is fluent in French. She likes to teach French language skills. In her
home, she has a room that could be used as an office.
1. Strength: Being able to speak French fluently
Interest: Teaching others
Other resource: A free room
2. The business idea: Open a small language school offering French courses
3. What else could she do to be unique: Organise a poetry competition in
French

WHAT YOU NEED TO DO
Identify Sources of Information
Self-Starting
Actively seek information. Don't wait to be given it.
Future-Oriented
Ask yourself: What sources of information will help me learn about future problems
and opportunities?
Overcoming Barriers
Identify at least one alternative to each information source you use!
Keep looking for information even if it is hard to find.
Use different sources of information, not just one.
Look for information that is rare and hard to come by. This information has the power
to innovate.
EXERCISE :
Identifying Sources of Information
Instruction:
1. Work in groups of four (04) people. Make a list of the sources of information you can use to
create innovative ideas. Can you find more than ten sources of information? Can you find
sources of information that the other groups cannot find? Write down all your ideas.
Examples of information sources:
o Websites
o Newspapers
2. Look at your list of information sources. What are the useful sources of information? How can
you use them to get innovative ideas for your business?
Example :
o Mobile phone accessories retailer
o Research websites to see how similar products are marketed in different Countries

WHAT YOU NEED TO DO
Identify Market Needs and Problems
Self-Starting
Think of three ways to identify needs and problems – they are opportunities!
Think of new features for existing products.
Look for weaknesses in competitors.
The Israelites said to them, “If only we had died by the Lord’s hand in Egypt! There we sat around pots
of meat and ate all the food we wanted, but you have brought us into this desert to starve this entire
community to death”.
Exodus 16: 3
WHAT YOU NEED TO DO
Identify Market Needs and Problems
Future-Oriented
Think of at least three ways your business can benefit from current changes that will
affect the market in future.
Overcoming Barriers
Barriers can be an opportunity for development
Think of at least three ways your business can turn a problem or need into an
opportunity.
PEOPLE HAVE NEEDS
To identify new business opportunities look for needs people have
by identifying:
What’s currently available is:
o Too expensive - Could I offer something cheaper?
o Not easy to use - Could I offer a more user-friendly version?
o The quality is very poor - Could I offer a better made product?
EXERCISE:
Problems are Opportunities
Instruction:
Work in groups of four (04).
1. Think about your community in Kenya, and identify the problems of its
population. Select the problems that have potential solutions (e.g.
"People don't have easy access to markets to sell their produce). What
can I do to solve this problem?). Also think about the problems that may
arise in the near future!
2. Choose a problem and find at least ten potential solutions.
3. How many of these solutions are entrepreneurial ideas?
